sources.title: PAC 140th report: Delhi Police audit and updated responses

sources.title: PAC 32nd action-taken report on Delhi Police
sources.publisher: Lok Sabha Secretariat, Public Accounts Committee
sources.locator: Introduction; chapter I p 1; printed pp 12, 20–21 and 36; Ministry final replies dated 30 January 2025
sources.summary: All twelve recommendations are categorized accepted by Government. Final replies update Safe City projected completion, CCTV maintenance committees and a ₹185 crore radio bid against ₹120 crore estimate.
limitations: Accepted recommendations do not mean every project was complete or every historic procurement issue resolved. The radio figure is a quoted bid, not a contract award or payment.

sources.title: Union Budget 2026–27: Demand 51, Police
sources.publisher: Ministry of Finance, Government of India
sources.locator: Printed pp 176–177, item 5 Delhi Police and item 14.02 Delhi Police infrastructure; explanatory notes
sources.summary: Separates 2024–25 actuals, 2025–26 BE/RE and 2026–27 BE for Delhi Police and the separate infrastructure scheme.
limitations: Already present in the retained force/union-home corpus; this city reader is explicit budget lineage, not newly alleged expenditure. Union Police demand totals and other forces are not Delhi spending.

sources.title: Delhi Police raising day: Safe City first phase inaugurated
sources.publisher: Press Information Bureau, Ministry of Home Affairs
sources.locator: Paragraph beginning “Union Home Minister said that today the foundation stones”; separate Special Cell project paragraph
sources.summary: Government announces first phase inauguration at about ₹857 crore, 2,100 new cameras live and integration of more than 15,000 existing cameras; separately announces ₹368 crore Special Cell headquarters project.
limitations: Official announcement, not audited final expenditure, full-project completion or evidence of effectiveness. ₹857 crore rounded announced project cost is not silently reconciled with the older ₹858 crore sanction. No operational-site details are mapped.

sources.title: Supreme Court: institutional safety review, 2026 INSC 1063
sources.locator: In Re: Recent Rape Incidents in Delhi NCR, SMW(Crl)6/2026; §8 no individual culpability determination; §9(v)(c) printed p8 Safe City functioning; §§10–12 measured reporting and infrastructure audit
sources.summary: Court seeks actual functioning, coverage and accountability for safety mechanisms including Safe City, rather than scheme names alone. Individual criminal culpability is expressly outside this institutional review.
limitations: Original official PDF retrieved and hashed. Only institutional extracts retained; sensitive incident narratives are excluded. Interim directions are not a corruption or vendor-liability finding.

sources.title: 5 October hearing: monitoring and implementation of Delhi safety measures
sources.locator: Opening institutional-monitoring paragraphs and final departmental-assurance / next-listing paragraphs
sources.summary: Reports the follow-up hearing, court questions on continuous monitoring and police counsel’s assurance that vigilance measures had been taken; reports next hearing on 16 November.
limitations: Reported hearing, not a retrieved 5 October written order. Oral remarks are not a final finding or proof of financial misconduct. No commercial article body or sensitive incident details retained.

records.title: Supreme Court asks whether Delhi safety schemes work on the ground
records.summary: The 28 September 2026 written order asks for the actual functioning and coverage of Safe City, ERSS112, Women Helpline181, Women Help Desks and One Stop Centres. It requires measurable implementation reporting and infrastructure audits. Section8 expressly says the proceedings do not determine individual criminal culpability. No missing-money or contractor-corruption conclusion follows from the direction.
records.dateBasis: Exact date of the retrieved written interim court order; not a criminal verdict or financial-loss finding.
records.period: Written interim institutional directions, 28 September 2026
records.response: The subsequent 5 October hearing is separately attributed to news reporting; a written compliance determination has not been retrieved. Government’s February 2026 first-phase inauguration remains material delivery context.
alternativeExplanations: An audit or procurement concern establishes the stated control issue, not bribery, diversion, a criminal conviction or a quantified financial loss.
records.falsifier: Revise on authenticated procurement files, reconciled ledgers, subsequent audit acceptance, contract completion records or a contrary court determination. A missing response is not an admission.

limitations: This proceeding concerns safety and institutional effectiveness, not adjudication of the financial audit cases. No survivor/accused identities, minor details or precise vulnerable sites are reproduced.

records.title: 5 October 2026 follow-up: monitoring questions and police assurances
records.summary: The Hindu reports that the Supreme Court questioned how CCTV installation prevents harm without continuous monitoring and sought practical implementation. Police counsel assured the court that several vigilance steps had been taken. The article reports a further hearing on 16 November 2026; that future date is not treated as an outcome.
records.dateBasis: Exact reported hearing date; written order not retrieved, no final guilt/compliance determination and no inference from the future listing.
records.period: Reported hearing, 5 October 2026
records.response: Departmental counsel’s assurance is retained. This is an attributed report of a hearing; the 5 October written order and resulting compliance report remain unverified.
